[[Robinson, Illinois]] | twitter = MLeonard_12 | former_school(s)= | career_highlights = | awards = | honors = *2009–2010 First-team [[Associated Press|AP]] Class 2A All-state (Illinois) | records = | championships = | championship_list = | tournaments = | tournament_list = | medal_templates = | medal_templates-expand = }} '''Meyers Leonard''' (born February 27, 1992) is an American [[basketball]] player who played two seasons at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]] before declaring his eligibility for the [[2012 NBA Draft|NBA Draft]] following the [[2011–12 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|2011–12 season]].{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/chicago/ncb/story/_/id/7767655/meyers-leonard-leave-illinois-fighting-illini-early-enter-nba-draft|title=Meyers Leonard to enter NBA draft |first=Scott |last=Powers |accessdate=April 3, 2012|date=April 13, 2012|publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]''}} ==Early life== Leonard's early life in [[Robinson, Illinois]], a small town roughly at the boundary between central and southern Illinois, was largely defined by family tragedy. When he was six years old, his father James, a golf pro, was killed in a freak bicycle accident. His mother Tracie, once an athlete capable of running as much as 10 miles a day, has been largely housebound since her husband's death, victimized by an old horseback injury and subsequent disc surgery that has left her with crippling pain.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7501291/illinois-fighting-illini-meyers-leonard-shoulders-plenty-college-basketball |title=Meyers Leonard shoulders plenty |first=Dana |last=O'Neil |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 25, 2012 |accessdate=January 25, 2012}} When he was in second grade, the young Leonard gained a surrogate family. Brian Siler, an insurance agent in Robinson who had a son of the same age, was aware of Leonard's family situation, and eventually became a father figure. Leonard regularly attended the Silers' church and went on family vacations. According to ''[[ESPN.com]]'' writer Dana O'Neil,
"Looking to shoehorn the relationship into a convenient box, outsiders have called this Meyers' version of ''The Blind Side'', but the comparison is inaccurate. [[The Blind Side: Evolution of a Game|The book]] and [[The Blind Side (film)|subsequent movie]] tell the story of [[Michael Oher]], a boy who was homeless and didn't have much of a family life. Meyers Leonard has a family. It has not abandoned him. On the contrary, Tracie loves her son, loves him so much that she was willing to accept help."
==High school== Leonard entered high school as a [[guard (basketball)|guard]], but was converted to center after a six-inch (15 cm) growth spurt between his freshman and sophomore years. O'Neil called him "something of a basketball anomaly", adding that Leonard "gained all that height without losing his coordination or his fast-twitch muscles." In high school, Leonard was named a member of the 2010 Illinois All-American Team as selected by the [[Associated Press]], [[Chicago Tribune]], [[Chicago Sun-Times]], [[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|News-Gazette]], and the Illinois Basketball Coaches Association. Leonard led Robinson High School to the [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] class 2A state championship {{cite web|title=Boys basketball Class 2A championship |url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-03-14/sports/chi-prep-bkb-2a-championship-march14_1_robinson-class-2a-championship-cashes |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=March 14, 2010}} before choosing to play collegiate basketball at the [[University of Illinois]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Meyers Leonard | position = C | hometown = Robinson, IL | highschool = Robinson High School | feet = 7 | inches = 0 | weight = 240 | 40 = | commitdate = 07/29/08 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2010 | rivals ref title = Illinois Commit List for 2010 | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN - Illinois Fighting Illini Basketball Recruiting 2010 | rivals school = 26 | scout s = 169 | espn schoolid = 356 | scout overall = 6 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | rivals overall = 6 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | espn overall = 4 ([[Center (basketball)|C]]) | accessdate = 2010-11-18 | bball = yes }} ==College== ===Freshman=== Entering the University of Illinois during the [[2010–11 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|2010–11 season]], Leonard averaged 2.1 points and 1.2 rebounds per game in 8.2 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Meyers Leonard |url=http://www.fightingillini.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/leonard_meyers00.html |work=FightingIllini.com}} ===Sophomore=== As a sophomore at the University of Illinois, Leonard averaged 13.6 points and 8.2 rebounds per game. Leonard was named Big 10 Co-Player of the Week on December 5, 2011 after averaging 16.5 points and 6.0 rebounds per game in two Illinois victories.{{cite web|title=Illinois, Indiana and Michigan State Claim Weekly Accolades|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/120511aaa.html|work=bigten.org|accessdate=26 June 2012}} Leonard was also named Big 10 Player of the Week on December 26, 2011 after averaging 16.5 points and 14.5 rebounds per game in two games.{{cite web|title=Leonard named Big 10 Player of the Week again|url=http://www.fightingillini.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/122611aaa.html|work=fightingillini.com|accessdate=26 June 2012}} Following the season, Leonard was named Honorable Mention All Big-10.{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/B1GMBB12Awards.pdf|title=2011-12 All-Big Ten Men’s Basketball Team|accessdate=2012-03-07|date=2012-06-26|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}} ===College Statistics=== {| class="wikitable" border="1" style="font-size: 90%;" |+ Career Statistics by Season |- !width=60 colspan="1" style="border-top-style:hidden;
